channelTitle: The plant Grandma June steeps has nothing to do with oatmeal
hook: This one has nothing to do with your morning oatmeal, but it comes from the very same plant.
remedy: As an old-fashioned piece of folk wisdom, the green stalks of the oat plant, dried and steeped as a mild tea, were sipped in the evening as a gentle way to unwind and settle a busy mind before bed.
steps: Steep a tablespoon of dried oat straw in a cup of hot water for 10 to 15 minutes
Sip warm in the evening, an hour or so before bed
caution: Skip this if you have a gluten sensitivity, since oat straw can carry trace gluten unless labeled certified gluten-free.
cta: Had you heard of oat straw tea before, or is chamomile still your go-to? Tell Grandma June in the comments.
